#PSYCH 221a Project
##Gabriel Hammond 



##Hypotheses

###H1: Male sex will predict higher rates of prior infection with disease (sum of pathogen prevalence scores) compared to female sex because testosterone suppresses immune function.

###H2: An increased degree of political difference in a relationship will predict lower relationship happiness because of the difficulty of reconciling opposing worldviews in domestic settings.


```{r Load packages and import data}
library(codebook)
library(tidyverse)


raw <- read.csv("Data/Raw_Data/data_doctored.csv")

#Pulling out the necessary variables 
data <- raw[,c("ResponseId","Sex_birth","Relationship_status",
                 "Pathogen_Prevalence_1","Pathogen_Prevalence_2",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_3","Pathogen_Prevalence_4",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_5","Pathogen_Prevalence_6",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_7","Pathogen_Prevalence_8",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_9","cot_politics_recoded","cpt_politics_recoded", "prqc_3"
               )]

dim(data)
str(data)


```




```{r participant_ids}

#count na

sum(is.na(data$ResponseId))

#count blank

sum(data$ResponseId=="",na.rm=TRUE)

#count duplicates

sum(duplicated(data$ResponseId))
summary(data$ResponseId)

#inspect records with missing or blank IDs

missingID <- which(is.na(data$ResponseId))
print(data[missingID,])

#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count

data <- data[!is.na(data$ResponseId),]

```

```{r sex_at_birth}
# codebook: 0 = Male, 1 = Female, 2 = Intersex

table(data$Sex_birth,useNA="ifany")

#turn Sex_birth into a factor with labels Male, Female, and Intersex

data$Sex_birth <- factor(data$Sex_birth,
                         levels = c(0,1,2),
                         labels = c("Male","Female","Intersex"))


```



```{r pathogen_prevalence}
#group the pathogen_prevalence_ variables and calculate total

pathvars <- c("Pathogen_Prevalence_1","Pathogen_Prevalence_2",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_3","Pathogen_Prevalence_4",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_5","Pathogen_Prevalence_6",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_7","Pathogen_Prevalence_8",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_9")

#see summary of variables

summary(data[,pathvars])

#count NAs

colSums(is.na(data[,pathvars]))


#Remove pathogen rows with NAs

path_cols <- c("Pathogen_Prevalence_1","Pathogen_Prevalence_2",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_3","Pathogen_Prevalence_4",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_5","Pathogen_Prevalence_6",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_7","Pathogen_Prevalence_8",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_9")

data_path <- data %>% drop_na(all_of(path_cols))

colSums(is.na(data_path[,pathvars]))

#Make sure pathogen scores are between 0 and 2

range(data_path[, c("Pathogen_Prevalence_1","Pathogen_Prevalence_2",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_3","Pathogen_Prevalence_4",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_5","Pathogen_Prevalence_6",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_7","Pathogen_Prevalence_8",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_9")], na.rm = TRUE)

#calculate summed pathogen score

data_path$path_sum <- rowSums(data_path[, c("Pathogen_Prevalence_1","Pathogen_Prevalence_2",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_3","Pathogen_Prevalence_4",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_5","Pathogen_Prevalence_6",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_7","Pathogen_Prevalence_8",
               "Pathogen_Prevalence_9")], na.rm = TRUE)

#values should range from 0-18 with no NAs 

summary(data_path$path_sum)

sum(is.na(data_path$path_sum))

#make h1Data with ID, Sex_birth, and path_sum

###JK: Keep participants with a pathogen score of zero; zero is a valid response, not a missing value. ###
# When you use path_sum directly as a condition, R treats 0 as FALSE and nonzero scores as TRUE.
# This removes everyone reporting no infection across the nine items.
# Replace the h1Data assignment below with an explicit missing-value check:
# h1Data <- data_path[
#   !is.na(data_path$path_sum) & !is.na(data_path$Sex_birth),
#   c("ResponseId", "Sex_birth", "path_sum")
# ]
# Then confirm that zero scores are retained:
# nrow(h1Data)
# sum(h1Data$path_sum == 0)
# range(h1Data$path_sum)
# With your current inclusion rules, H1 should contain 97,369 participants, including those with zero scores.
###  End of comment ###

h1Data <- data_path[data_path$path_sum & !is.na(data_path$Sex_birth), c("ResponseId","Sex_birth","path_sum")]

```

```{r validate politics variables and calculate political difference}

polvars <- c("cot_politics_recoded","cpt_politics_recoded", "prqc_3", "Relationship_status")

#see summary of variables

summary(data[,polvars])

#count NAs

colSums(is.na(data[,polvars]))


#Remove political rows with NAs

pol_cols <- c("cot_politics_recoded","cpt_politics_recoded", "prqc_3", "Relationship_status")

data_pol <- data %>% drop_na(all_of(pol_cols))

colSums(is.na(data_pol[,polvars]))

#convert self political descriptions from text to numeric

data_pol$cot_politics_recoded <- 
  ifelse(data_pol$cot_politics_recoded == "far left political views", 1,
                                        ifelse(data_pol$cot_politics_recoded == "center left political views",2,
                                               ifelse(data_pol$cot_politics_recoded == "center political views",3,
                                                      ifelse(data_pol$cot_politics_recoded == "center right political views",4,
                                                             ifelse(data_pol$cot_politics_recoded == "far right political views", 5,data_pol$cot_politics_recoded))
                                                 
                                               )))
#make sure it's numeric

data_pol$cot_politics_recoded <- as.numeric(data_pol$cot_politics_recoded)


#do the same for partner political descriptions 

data_pol$cpt_politics_recoded <- ifelse(data_pol$cpt_politics_recoded == "far left political views", 1,
                                 ifelse(data_pol$cpt_politics_recoded == "center left political views", 2,
                                 ifelse(data_pol$cpt_politics_recoded == "center political views", 3,
                                 ifelse(data_pol$cpt_politics_recoded == "center right political views", 4,
                                 ifelse(data_pol$cpt_politics_recoded == "far right political views", 5, 
                                        data_pol$cpt_politics_recoded)))))

#make sure it's numeric

data_pol$cpt_politics_recoded <- as.numeric(data_pol$cpt_politics_recoded)


#calculate political difference score

data_pol$pol_diff <- data_pol$cot_politics_recoded - data_pol$cpt_politics_recoded

#check range of values, should go from -4 to 4

summary(data_pol$pol_diff)

#convert to absolute difference
data_pol$pol_diff <- abs(data_pol$pol_diff)

summary(data_pol$pol_diff)

#make h2Data with ID, political vars, prqc_3, and Relationship_status

###JK: The same issue occurs here: a political difference of zero means matching political views and should be retained. ###
# Using pol_diff directly as a condition drops all 32,169 participants whose political views match their partner's.
# Replace the h2Data assignment below with:
# h2Data <- data_pol[
#   !is.na(data_pol$pol_diff) & !is.na(data_pol$Relationship_status) & !is.na(data_pol$prqc_3),
#   c("ResponseId", "cot_politics_recoded", "cpt_politics_recoded", "prqc_3", "Relationship_status", "pol_diff")
# ]
# Check that the full 0-4 difference range is represented:
# table(h2Data$pol_diff, useNA = "ifany")
# nrow(h2Data)
# With your current inclusion rules, H2 should contain 48,250 participants before any additional relationship-status restriction.
###  End of comment ###

###JK: I recommend keeping relationship statuses 1 (Dating), 2 (Committed relationship), and 3 (Married) for H2. ###
# 0 means Single.
# Some participants who reported being single also answered prqc_3, the relationship happiness question.
# I checked the original codebook, but I could not find an explanation for why they answered it.
# It is up to you, but since your hypothesis concerns people in relationships, I recommend using only statuses 1, 2, and 3.
# If you follow this recommendation, add the following line AFTER creating the corrected h2Data:
# h2Data <- h2Data[h2Data$Relationship_status %in% c(1, 2, 3), ]
# table(h2Data$Relationship_status, useNA = "ifany")
# Please also describe your decision in your codebook or inclusion notes.
###  End of comment ###

h2Data <- data_pol[data_pol$pol_diff & !is.na(data_pol$Relationship_status) & !is.na(data_pol$prqc_3), c("ResponseId", "cot_politics_recoded","cpt_politics_recoded", "prqc_3", "Relationship_status", "pol_diff")]

```

```{r variable_labels}
#description of each h1Data column, in column order
var_label(h1Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Sex at birth: original codes 0=Male, 1=Female, 2=Intersex; now stored as a factor",
  "Prior infection to specific pathogens, where 0 = no infection and 18 = repeated infection with 9 pathogens"
)

#add a description to each h2Data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule
var_label(h2Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Political views of self where far left political views = 1, center left political views = 2, center political views = 3, center right political views = 4, and far right political views = 5",
  "Political views of partner where far left political views = 1, center left political views = 2, center political views = 3, center right political views = 4, and far right political views = 5",
  "Relationship Satisfaction: How happy are you in your relationship? Values range from 1 (low) to 7 (high)",
  "Relationship Status: Single (0), Dating (1), In a committed relationship (2), Married (3)",
  "Political Difference, reflecting the absolute difference between self and partner's political beliefs"
)

```

```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save h1Data and h2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(h1Data,"data/processed_data/h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(h2Data,"data/processed_data/h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h2.csv")
dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)

```
